rounds.text: Aptech Ltd presents a compelling case for undervaluation as its fundamental performance significantly outpaces its current market pricing. The company is trading at a P/E of 18.1x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 9.93x [E11], both of which sit below their respective sector benchmarks [E6, E11]. Efficiency metrics are particularly strong, with an ROCE of 16.92% [E10] and an ROA of 6.54% [E8] both comfortably exceeding sector benchmarks [E8, E10]. The business is effectively debt-free [E59] and generates robust cash, with profits fully backed by operating cash flow [E34] and a completed capital expenditure cycle [E40]. While the stock has suffered from negative institutional money flow [E44] and a poor technical trend [E50, E51], the intrinsic value suggested by a discounted cash flow model sits at Rs 144 per share, implying a significant margin of safety of 44.4% [E45, E46]. Conceded: the stock has experienced a compounded share price decline of 28% over the last year [E25] and institutional holdings have decreased since 2023 [E42, E43]. Despite this, the company is demonstrating a clear turnaround with 23% profit growth in the trailing twelve months [E21] and a healthy dividend yield of 5.62% [E4, E60].
